Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

Class DatumList

java.lang.Object
java.util.AbstractCollection<E>
java.util.AbstractList<E>
java.util.AbstractSequentialList<Datum>
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.DatumList
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<Datum>, Collection<Datum>, List<Datum>
public final class DatumList extends AbstractSequentialList<Datum> implements Iterable<Datum>
List view into a datum. Elements of a list are the cars along its cdr chain. The final non-cons datum (known as the terminator) is accessible at tail().

The terminator is not considered an element of the list, so Java list operations such as equality and hash code are not affected by its value.

DatumList is read-only because datums are immutable.

Since:
0.1.0

      public DatumList(List<? extends Datum> list)

    • finish

      public void finish(DatumWalk iter)
      Consumes a datum iterator and updates this list’s length and terminator from its states. It is ideal if the iterator has been partially or fully consumed.

      Of course, the iterator has to be iterating from the same root datum as the one this list is viewing.

      Parameters:
      iter - iterator
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if iter is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the iterator is iterating from a different root datum

    • isProperList

      public final boolean isProperList()
      Returns whether this list is proper. A list is proper if and only if its terminator tail() is nil.

      If you are doing this as a part of validation, consider the stricter requireProperTail().

      Returns:
      whether this list is proper

    • toProperList

      public DatumList toProperList()
      Returns a view of the same elements, terminated by nil. If this list is already proper, this is returned as is; otherwise the elements are copied into a new chain.
      Returns:
      a view of the same elements, terminated by nil
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if you have a mega list with length exceeding Integer.MAX_VALUE; I think this should be rare, but still be careful!
